title: Some mathematicians call for OpenAI boycott after AI-generated proofs flood their field
key_facts: The Association for Human Mathematics (AHM) is calling for a boycott of OpenAI after the company published hundreds of AI-generated mathematical manuscripts.
AHM accuses OpenAI of violating core norms of scientific research and urges mathematicians to stop working with the company.
Fields Medalist Terence Tao chairs the group and shared the statement as a guest post on his blog.
The statement calls the release of more than 700 files at once not a demonstration of scholarship but a demonstration of power.
Scott Aaronson called the situation a "Mathocalypse"; his wife Dana Moshkovitz said one claimed proof is impossible to read without AI help.
The advisory group AGMAI (Institute for Advanced Study) takes a milder line, calling the release a first step.
Comments on Tao's blog are divided: some back the boycott, others call it unrealistic.
Aaronson, citing unnamed sources, says AI companies are quietly probing cryptographic protocols; this is unconfirmed.
quote_evidence: The Association for Human Mathematics (AHM) accuses OpenAI of violating core norms of scientific research by publishing the AI proofs and is urging mathematicians to stop working with the company.

Fields Medalist Terence Tao, who chairs the group, shared the statement as a guest post on his blog, while also outlining a "Math 2.0" era on Mastodon in which solving problems should no longer be the main focus of the discipline.
Comments on Tao's blog post show how divided the field is.
why_it_matters_hint: Hundreds of AI-written proofs now have to be checked by humans, and a leading group wants researchers to withdraw from working with OpenAI.
event_date: AHM statement released 7 Oct 2026 (per Retraction Watch); OpenAI release 6 Oct 2026
